what_happened: In job 38jx, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The request was for a design review that runs every 10 landed jobs. The reading did not say that no design-review role exists yet. The user restated that the request queued by the cadence must therefore carry its whole content. It must say what to review: the code-health table, the files most changed and most broken since the last review, open structural-pass requests, and recent rejections and planning stops. It must say what to produce: a short design note with proposed changes, run as a design-only job.
cause: The reading stage works from the request text and does not check which roles, files and capabilities exist in the current snapshot. It treated a design-review role as something the queued request could rely on, so the request's content was left implicit. Nothing compares a reading's assumed capabilities with the repo before the reading is accepted. The user is the only one who knows the role is absent, and the same kind of correction will recur for any cadence or scheduled request that names a missing role.
prevention: Add a check before a reading is accepted. It lists the roles, prompts and files the reading depends on and confirms each exists in the current snapshot. When one is missing, the check requires the reading either to make any request it queues self-contained (scope, inputs and output form stated in the request body) or to add the missing role as a deliverable. A request created by a cadence or other automatic trigger must pass a self-containment test: it can be read and carried out with no role-specific prompt.
proposed_request: Add a design-review cadence: after every 10 landed jobs, Athena queues one design-only job. No design-review role exists, so the queued request must carry its whole content in its body. It must tell the job to review the code-health table, the files most changed and most broken since the last review, open structural-pass requests, and recent rejections and planning stops. It must tell the job to produce a short design note with proposed changes. Acceptance: (1) a test lands 10 jobs and shows exactly one such request is queued, and none after 9; (2) a test shows the queued request text names every review input above and the design-note output, and is classed as design-only; (3) the count restarts from the last review; (4) no new role or prompt file is added; (5) the request text avoids words the boundary scan bans.
